description: From 1 July 2022 the permitted share of foreigners per neighbourhood was cut from 25% to 20%, closing roughly 1,200 districts to new primary residence permits. If your address is in a closed zone the application is automatically rejected.

The policy responded to an influx of migrants into popular regions, with the increase from Iraq and Iran cited alongside Russians. The rule is address-based, but the population it was written about is named.
energy_note: Neutral on its face, aimed in its explanation.

aspect: EXAMPLE - eight Istanbul districts at once
description: On 7 October 2022 the Interior Minister closed residence permits in eight Istanbul districts - Kucukcekmece, Basaksehir, Bagcilar, Avcilar, Bahcelievler, Sultangazi, Esenler and Zeytinburnu - with no new foreigner registration allowed.

aspect: EXAMPLE - rent first, find out after
description: Buying or renting property in a closed area remains possible - only the permit is refused. A family can sign a lease and then discover the address disqualifies them from living there lawfully.
money_note: A lease that cannot produce a permit.

description: Reporting suggests most districts reopened around June 2026, except Fatih and Esenyurt in Istanbul - while other 2026 guidance claims the opposite, that rules tightened, income verification hardened and restricted neighbourhoods increased. The current picture is genuinely contested.
energy_note: Nobody can tell you what the rule is this month.

aspect: SCENARIO - the lease and the postcode
description: Omid and Maryam sign a twelve-month lease in Esenyurt because it is what they can afford. The residence permit application is rejected automatically: the district is closed. They are lawfully renting an address at which they may not lawfully reside.
